blocks.text: For SFO–Bangkok on January 15, the most straightforward award choice is a one-ticket economy itinerary that leaves late that evening and reaches Bangkok the morning of January 17. If getting in earlier matters more than avoiding a much earlier start, another one-ticket economy option arrives late on January 16. A third possibility reaches business class, but it requires a separate positioning flight to Los Angeles and a far earlier departure from San Francisco.
The late-departure choice: the displayed schedule gets you to Bangkok at 9:50 a.m. on January 17.
blocks.label: Late SFO departure

blocks.text: Compared with that option, this earlier-arrival alternative lands at 10:25 p.m. on January 16—1 hour 25 minutes earlier—but leaves SFO at 11:45 a.m. instead of 11:15 p.m. on January 15. Both are economy awards through Aeroplan, so this is a schedule trade rather than a cabin upgrade.
Choose this if the earlier Bangkok arrival justifies leaving San Francisco substantially earlier.
blocks.label: Earlier Bangkok arrival

blocks.text: For a business-class possibility, the LAX itinerary arrives at 8:50 a.m. on January 17, later than the two direct-award choices, and requires leaving SFO at 6:18 a.m. It therefore trades a much earlier start and a separate positioning leg for the higher cabin. The schedule is a distinct choice, not a simple upgrade to the late SFO departure.
The award portion is reported in business; the separate positioning leg and its risks are important parts of the overall trip.
blocks.label: Business via Los Angeles

claims.text: Award journey-level business cabin evidence only

blocks.text: For context, the end-to-end cash search returned a $440 SFO–Bangkok itinerary departing January 15 and arriving January 17. It is a separate cash baseline, not an award, and its returned one-traveler search result does not establish a party price scope.
A cash-search reference for the requested endpoint pair, rather than a nonstop-only benchmark.
blocks.label: SFO–Bangkok cash search

blocks.text: The award observations are dated October 9, 2026, not live availability. The direct award quotes show taxes but have unknown price scope, so they do not establish a complete all-in price for your party. The LAX option’s award taxes are unavailable and the positioning fare is not a complete trip price. Because its positioning flight and award are separate tickets, baggage, check-in, terminal or transit requirements, and missed-connection protection need verification; that added exposure is part of the trade-off. The LAX business cabin evidence applies to the award portion, not necessarily the positioning flight.
